summary: Moons around Jupiter, phases of Venus and mountains on the Moon: the heavens were neither perfect nor Earth-centred.
body:
Part of [The Scientific Revolution](event:scientific-revolution). His advocacy of [Copernicus](event:copernicus) brought him before the Inquisition in 1633 and house arrest for the rest of his life.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galileo_Galilei).

name: Kepler's laws of planetary motion
summary: Planets move in ellipses, sweeping equal areas in equal times — the first mathematically exact astronomy.
body:
Part of [The Scientific Revolution](event:scientific-revolution). Planets move in ellipses, sweeping equal areas in equal times — the first mathematically exact astronomy.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kepler%27s_laws_of_planetary_motion).

name: Newton's Principia
summary: Three laws of motion and universal gravitation explained falling bodies, tides, comets and planetary orbits with one system.
body:
Part of [The Scientific Revolution](event:scientific-revolution). Newton also invented calculus to do it. The *Principia* is arguably the most influential scientific book ever written, and it made physics the model to which every other science aspired for two hundred years.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philosophiæ_Naturalis_Principia_Mathematica).

name: Mughal Empire
summary: Babur's descendants ruled most of the Indian subcontinent, at their height the richest state in the world.
body:
Akbar's religious tolerance and administrative reforms, and the architecture of Shah Jahan including the [Taj Mahal](event:taj-mahal), mark the empire's high point; the [British East India Company](event:british-raj) picked over its decline.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mughal_Empire).

name: Taj Mahal built
summary: Shah Jahan built a white marble mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz Mahal on the Yamuna.
body:
Part of [Mughal Empire](event:mughal-empire). Shah Jahan built a white marble mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz Mahal on the Yamuna.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taj_Mahal).

name: Little Ice Age
summary: A few tenths of a degree of cooling brought advancing glaciers, frozen rivers and repeated harvest failures across the northern hemisphere.
body:
Solar minima, volcanic eruptions and possibly American [reforestation after depopulation](event:americas-epidemics) all contributed. The Thames froze hard enough for frost fairs; Norse Greenland was abandoned.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Ice_Age).

name: Battle of Lepanto
summary: A Holy League fleet destroyed the Ottoman navy in the last great battle fought mainly by oared galleys.
body:
Part of [Ottoman Empire](event:ottoman-empire). A Holy League fleet destroyed the Ottoman navy in the last great battle fought mainly by oared galleys.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Lepanto).

name: Defeat of the Spanish Armada
summary: Philip II's invasion fleet was scattered by English fireships and Atlantic storms.
body:
Part of [Protestant Reformation](event:reformation). Philip II's invasion fleet was scattered by English fireships and Atlantic storms.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Armada).

name: Shakespeare's plays
summary: Thirty-seven plays written for a London commercial theatre became the central works of English literature.
body:
Thirty-seven plays written for a London commercial theatre became the central works of English literature.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Shakespeare).

name: Tokugawa Japan and sakoku
summary: The Tokugawa shogunate imposed two and a half centuries of internal peace and near-total isolation from the outside world.
body:
Foreign trade was restricted to a single Dutch outpost at Nagasaki until American gunboats forced the country open, precipitating the [Meiji Restoration](event:meiji).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edo_period).

name: English Civil War
summary: Parliament defeated and then executed Charles I, the first European monarch tried and beheaded by his own subjects.
body:
Parliament defeated and then executed Charles I, the first European monarch tried and beheaded by his own subjects.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_Civil_War).

name: Qing dynasty
summary: Manchu rulers conquered Ming China and expanded it to its greatest territorial extent, before collapsing under internal revolt and foreign pressure.
body:
The [Taiping Rebellion](event:taiping) and the [Opium Wars](event:opium-wars) hollowed out the dynasty; it fell in 1912.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qing_dynasty).

name: Glorious Revolution
summary: Parliament invited William of Orange to replace James II, and attached a Bill of Rights to the crown.
body:
Constitutional monarchy, parliamentary supremacy and the Bank of England follow from this settlement.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glorious_Revolution).

name: Ottoman siege of Vienna
summary: A Polish-led relief army broke the siege, marking the high-water mark of Ottoman expansion in Europe.
body:
Part of [Ottoman Empire](event:ottoman-empire). A Polish-led relief army broke the siege, marking the high-water mark of Ottoman expansion in Europe.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Vienna).

name: The Enlightenment
summary: European thinkers argued that reason, evidence and individual rights, not tradition or revelation, should organise society.
body:
Locke, Voltaire, Hume, Rousseau, Kant, Smith and Diderot were read across a continent-wide republic of letters. Their arguments underwrote the [American](event:american-revolution) and [French](event:french-revolution) revolutions, the abolition of the [slave trade](event:slave-trade), and the idea of progress itself.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Age_of_Enlightenment).

name: Adam Smith, The Wealth of Nations
summary: The founding text of economics argued that specialisation and free exchange, not hoarded bullion, create national wealth.
body:
Part of [The Enlightenment](event:enlightenment). The founding text of economics argued that specialisation and free exchange, not hoarded bullion, create national wealth.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wealth_of_Nations).

name: Lisbon earthquake
summary: An earthquake, tsunami and fire destroyed one of Europe's great capitals on All Saints' Day.
body:
Tens of thousands died. The disaster shook Enlightenment optimism — Voltaire's *Candide* is a direct response — and prompted the first systematic scientific survey of an earthquake.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1755_Lisbon_earthquake).

name: Seven Years' War
summary: A war fought in Europe, North America, the Caribbean, West Africa, India and the Philippines — arguably the first global conflict.
body:
Britain took Canada and effective control of Bengal; the debts it ran up led it to tax the American colonies, with consequences it did not expect.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_Years%27_War).

name: Industrial Revolution
summary: Machines powered by coal replaced muscle, and for the first time in history sustained economic growth outran population growth.
body:
It began with textiles and [steam](event:watt-engine) in Britain, spread to iron, chemicals and [railways](event:railways), and within a century had remade work, cities, class and warfare.

Human living standards, life expectancy and energy use all bend sharply upward from this point — as does atmospheric CO2, the beginning of [modern climate change](event:global-warming).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industrial_Revolution).

name: Mechanised spinning
summary: Hargreaves' spinning jenny and Arkwright's water frame multiplied the output of a single worker many times over.
body:
Part of [Industrial Revolution](event:industrial-revolution). Hargreaves' spinning jenny and Arkwright's water frame multiplied the output of a single worker many times over.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spinning_jenny).

name: Watt's steam engine
summary: A separate condenser made the steam engine efficient enough to power factories anywhere, not just to pump out mines.
body:
Part of [Industrial Revolution](event:industrial-revolution). A separate condenser made the steam engine efficient enough to power factories anywhere, not just to pump out mines.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watt_steam_engine).

name: First passenger railway
summary: The Liverpool and Manchester Railway opened, the first intercity line worked entirely by steam locomotives.
body:
Part of [Industrial Revolution](event:industrial-revolution). Within thirty years rail networks covered Britain, Europe and the eastern United States, collapsing travel times and forcing the adoption of standard time.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_and_Manchester_Railway).

name: American Revolution
summary: Thirteen British colonies declared themselves independent and, with French help, made it stick.
body:
The [Declaration of Independence](event:declaration-independence) asserted that governments derive their just powers from the consent of the governed; victory at [Yorktown](event:yorktown) secured it, and the [Constitution](event:us-constitution) of 1787 turned it into a working federal republic.

The example — and the debts France ran up supporting it — helped bring on the [French Revolution](event:french-revolution).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Revolution).

name: Declaration of Independence
summary: The Continental Congress adopted Jefferson's declaration that all men are created equal and endowed with unalienable rights.
body:
Part of [American Revolution](event:american-revolution). The Continental Congress adopted Jefferson's declaration that all men are created equal and endowed with unalienable rights.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Declaration_of_Independence).

name: Siege of Yorktown
summary: A Franco-American army and a French fleet trapped Cornwallis, effectively ending the war.
body:
Part of [American Revolution](event:american-revolution). A Franco-American army and a French fleet trapped Cornwallis, effectively ending the war.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Yorktown).

name: United States Constitution
summary: A written constitution with separated powers, federalism and (from 1791) a Bill of Rights.
body:
Part of [American Revolution](event:american-revolution). It is the oldest national constitution still in force, and the model for most written constitutions since.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_the_United_States).

name: French Revolution
summary: The old European order of monarchy, aristocracy and established church was overthrown in its most powerful state.
body:
From the storming of the [Bastille](event:bastille) and the [Declaration of the Rights of Man](event:rights-of-man) through the [Terror](event:terror) to [Napoleon's coup](event:napoleon-coup), the revolution ran through every political possibility in ten years.

It exported the vocabulary of modern politics — left and right, nation, citizen, ideology — and its wars remade Europe as the [Napoleonic Wars](event:napoleonic-wars).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Revolution).

name: Storming of the Bastille
summary: A Paris crowd took the royal fortress-prison on 14 July, still France's national day.
body:
Part of [French Revolution](event:french-revolution). A Paris crowd took the royal fortress-prison on 14 July, still France's national day.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storming_of_the_Bastille).

name: Declaration of the Rights of Man
summary: Liberty, property, security and resistance to oppression declared the natural rights of every man.
body:
Part of [French Revolution](event:french-revolution). Liberty, property, security and resistance to oppression declared the natural rights of every man.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen).

name: The Reign of Terror
summary: The Committee of Public Safety executed some 17,000 people, including the king, the queen and finally Robespierre.
body:
Part of [French Revolution](event:french-revolution). The Committee of Public Safety executed some 17,000 people, including the king, the queen and finally Robespierre.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reign_of_Terror).

name: Napoleon seizes power
summary: The coup of 18 Brumaire ended the Directory and made Bonaparte First Consul; he crowned himself emperor in 1804.
body:
Part of [French Revolution](event:french-revolution). The coup of 18 Brumaire ended the Directory and made Bonaparte First Consul; he crowned himself emperor in 1804.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coup_of_18_Brumaire).

name: Haitian Revolution
summary: Enslaved people in France's richest colony overthrew their masters and founded the first Black republic.
body:
Toussaint Louverture's army defeated French, Spanish and British forces. It is the only successful large-scale slave revolt in modern history, and it terrified slaveholding societies everywhere — see the [Atlantic slave trade](event:slave-trade).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haitian_Revolution).

name: Jenner's smallpox vaccine
summary: Edward Jenner showed that cowpox inoculation protects against smallpox, founding vaccination.
body:
The technique eventually [eradicated smallpox](event:smallpox-eradication) — the only human disease ever deliberately wiped out.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smallpox_vaccine).

name: Napoleonic Wars
summary: France under Napoleon fought most of Europe for twelve years and briefly dominated the continent.
body:
Part of [French Revolution](event:french-revolution). Nelson's victory at [Trafalgar](event:trafalgar) secured British command of the sea; the [invasion of Russia](event:russia-1812) destroyed the Grande Armée; [Waterloo](event:waterloo) ended the adventure.

The wars spread the Napoleonic Code, conscription and nationalism across Europe, and the peace that followed at Vienna held the great powers back from general war for a century — until [1914](event:ww1).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleonic_Wars).

name: Battle of Trafalgar
summary: Nelson destroyed the combined French and Spanish fleets off Cadiz, ending any prospect of invading Britain.
body:
Part of [Napoleonic Wars](event:napoleonic-wars). Nelson destroyed the combined French and Spanish fleets off Cadiz, ending any prospect of invading Britain.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Trafalgar).

name: Battle of Austerlitz
summary: Napoleon's masterpiece: a feigned weakness drew the Austro-Russian army onto ground of his choosing.
body:
Part of [Napoleonic Wars](event:napoleonic-wars). Napoleon's masterpiece: a feigned weakness drew the Austro-Russian army onto ground of his choosing.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Austerlitz).

name: French invasion of Russia
summary: An army of some 600,000 marched to Moscow; fewer than a tenth came back.
body:
Part of [Napoleonic Wars](event:napoleonic-wars). An army of some 600,000 marched to Moscow; fewer than a tenth came back.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_invasion_of_Russia).

name: Battle of Waterloo
summary: Wellington held the ridge until the Prussians arrived; Napoleon abdicated four days later and died in exile on St Helena.
body:
Part of [Napoleonic Wars](event:napoleonic-wars). Wellington held the ridge until the Prussians arrived; Napoleon abdicated four days later and died in exile on St Helena.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Waterloo).

name: Latin American wars of independence
summary: Spain and Portugal lost almost all of their American empires within a generation.
body:
Bolívar and San Martín campaigned from Venezuela to Peru; Brazil separated from Portugal without a general war. The new republics inherited enormous inequality and unstable borders.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_American_wars_of_independence).

name: Eruption of Tambora
summary: The largest eruption in recorded history threw enough sulphate into the stratosphere to cool the whole planet.
body:
Tens of thousands died on Sumbawa; far more died in the [famines of the following year](event:year-without-summer).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1815_eruption_of_Mount_Tambora).

name: The Year Without a Summer
summary: Snow fell in New England in June and harvests failed across Europe and Asia, causing the worst famine of the century.
body:
Part of [Eruption of Tambora](event:tambora). Kept indoors by the weather at Lake Geneva, Mary Shelley wrote *Frankenstein*.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Year_Without_a_Summer).

name: Opium Wars
summary: Britain forced China to keep importing opium, taking Hong Kong and a series of unequal treaties.
body:
The wars began the "century of humiliation" that ended imperial China and shaped Chinese foreign policy to this day.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opium_Wars).

name: Taiping Rebellion
summary: A millenarian movement led by a man who believed he was Jesus's younger brother held southern China for a decade; 20–30 million died.
body:
It is among the deadliest wars in history, and it broke the finances and the prestige of the [Qing](event:qing-dynasty).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiping_Rebellion).

name: Electric telegraph
summary: Morse's Washington–Baltimore line separated communication from transport for the first time in history.
body:
By 1866 a working cable crossed the Atlantic, cutting the time for a message from London to New York from ten days to minutes.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrical_telegraph).

name: Revolutions of 1848
summary: Liberal and nationalist uprisings swept some fifty European states within months; nearly all were suppressed within two years.
body:
Liberal and nationalist uprisings swept some fifty European states within months; nearly all were suppressed within two years.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolutions_of_1848).

name: The Communist Manifesto
summary: Marx and Engels published a short pamphlet arguing that history is driven by class struggle.
body:
It became the founding text of a movement that would govern a third of humanity in the twentieth century — see the [Russian Revolution](event:russian-revolution) and [the founding of the PRC](event:prc-founded).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Communist_Manifesto).

name: Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species
summary: Natural selection explained the diversity and design of life without a designer.
body:
Darwin had sat on the idea for twenty years; Alfred Russel Wallace's independent arrival at the same conclusion forced publication. The theory unified all of biology and, with [genetics](event:dna-structure), remains its central organising principle.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On_the_Origin_of_Species).

name: Germ theory of disease
summary: Pasteur, Koch and Lister established that specific microorganisms cause specific diseases.
body:
Antisepsis, pasteurisation, sterile surgery and public sanitation followed; combined with later [antibiotics](event:penicillin) and [vaccination](event:smallpox-vaccine), they roughly doubled human life expectancy.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germ_theory_of_disease).

name: American Civil War
summary: The United States fought its bloodiest war over slavery and secession; some 700,000 died.
body:
The [Emancipation Proclamation](event:emancipation) turned the war into a war against [slavery](event:slave-trade); [Gettysburg](event:gettysburg) broke the Confederate offensive; [Lincoln was assassinated](event:lincoln-assassination) days after the surrender at Appomattox.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Civil_War).

name: Emancipation Proclamation
summary: Lincoln declared enslaved people in the rebelling states to be free; the Thirteenth Amendment abolished slavery outright in 1865.
body:
Part of [American Civil War](event:us-civil-war). Lincoln declared enslaved people in the rebelling states to be free; the Thirteenth Amendment abolished slavery outright in 1865.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emancipation_Proclamation).

name: Battle of Gettysburg
summary: Three days of fighting in Pennsylvania ended Lee's invasion of the North.
body:
Part of [American Civil War](event:us-civil-war). Three days of fighting in Pennsylvania ended Lee's invasion of the North.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Gettysburg).

name: Assassination of Abraham Lincoln
summary: Lincoln was shot at Ford's Theatre five days after Lee's surrender.
body:
Part of [American Civil War](event:us-civil-war). Lincoln was shot at Ford's Theatre five days after Lee's surrender.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Abraham_Lincoln).

name: Meiji Restoration
summary: Japan abolished the shogunate and deliberately industrialised, becoming a great power within a generation.
body:
Within forty years of [ending its isolation](event:edo-japan) Japan had defeated Russia at sea — the first modern victory of an Asian state over a European empire.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meiji_Restoration).

name: British Raj
summary: The Crown took over direct rule of India from the East India Company after the rebellion of 1857.
body:
Railways, telegraphs and English-language institutions coexisted with deindustrialisation and repeated devastating famines. It ended with [independence and partition](event:indian-independence).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj).

name: Suez Canal opens
summary: A sea-level canal between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea cut thousands of kilometres from the Europe–Asia route.
body:
A sea-level canal between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea cut thousands of kilometres from the Europe–Asia route.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suez_Canal).

name: First transcontinental railroad
summary: The golden spike at Promontory Summit joined the American rail network coast to coast.
body:
Part of [First passenger railway](event:railways). The golden spike at Promontory Summit joined the American rail network coast to coast.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_transcontinental_railroad).

name: Mendeleev's periodic table
summary: Arranging the elements by weight and property revealed a periodic law — and gaps where undiscovered elements had to be.
body:
Arranging the elements by weight and property revealed a periodic law — and gaps where undiscovered elements had to be.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periodic_table).

name: Telephone
summary: Alexander Graham Bell patented a device that carried the human voice over a wire.
body:
Alexander Graham Bell patented a device that carried the human voice over a wire.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telephone).

name: Practical electric lighting
summary: Edison's long-lasting incandescent lamp, and the generating stations built to supply it, electrified cities.
body:
Edison's long-lasting incandescent lamp, and the generating stations built to supply it, electrified cities.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incandescent_light_bulb).

name: Eruption of Krakatoa
summary: The explosion was heard 4,800 km away and the tsunamis it raised killed more than 36,000 people.
body:
It was the first global disaster reported worldwide within hours, by [telegraph](event:telegraph).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1883_eruption_of_Krakatoa).

name: Scramble for Africa
summary: European powers partitioned almost the entire African continent among themselves in three decades.
body:
The Berlin Conference of 1884–85 set the rules; the borders drawn then are largely those of Africa today. Conquest was brutal — the Congo Free State alone may have cost millions of lives — and was undone only by [decolonisation](event:decolonisation) after 1945.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scramble_for_Africa).

name: First powered flight
summary: The Wright brothers flew a heavier-than-air powered machine under control at Kitty Hawk.
body:
Sixty-six years separate that 12-second hop from the [Moon landing](event:moon-landing).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wright_Flyer).

name: Einstein's theory of relativity
summary: Space and time turned out to be aspects of one flexible geometry, and mass a form of energy.
body:
Special relativity (1905) fixed the incompatibility between mechanics and electromagnetism; general relativity (1915) recast gravity as the curvature of spacetime, and was confirmed by the bending of starlight in 1919.

GPS, black holes, cosmology and [gravitational waves](event:gravitational-waves) all follow from it.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theory_of_relativity).

name: World War I
summary: Four years of industrial-scale war killed some 20 million people and destroyed four empires.
body:
An [assassination in Sarajevo](event:sarajevo) triggered interlocking alliances; machine guns and artillery made the [Western Front](event:somme) a stalemate of trenches for four years. Russia collapsed into [revolution](event:russian-revolution); the United States entered in 1917.

The [Treaty of Versailles](event:versailles) redrew Europe and the Middle East, and left grievances that contributed directly to [the next war](event:ww2).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I).

name: Assassination of Franz Ferdinand
summary: Gavrilo Princip shot the Austrian heir in Sarajevo, setting off the July Crisis.
body:
Part of [World War I](event:ww1). Gavrilo Princip shot the Austrian heir in Sarajevo, setting off the July Crisis.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Archduke_Franz_Ferdinand).

name: Battle of Verdun
summary: Ten months of attrition around a French fortress city cost some 700,000 casualties.
body:
Part of [World War I](event:ww1). Ten months of attrition around a French fortress city cost some 700,000 casualties.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Verdun).

name: Battle of the Somme
summary: Nearly 60,000 British casualties fell on the first day; tanks appeared in battle for the first time.
body:
Part of [World War I](event:ww1). Nearly 60,000 British casualties fell on the first day; tanks appeared in battle for the first time.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_the_Somme).

name: Treaty of Versailles
summary: The peace imposed on Germany assigned it war guilt and reparations, and redrew the map of Europe.
body:
Part of [World War I](event:ww1). The peace imposed on Germany assigned it war guilt and reparations, and redrew the map of Europe.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Versailles).

name: Russian Revolution
summary: Tsarism fell and the Bolsheviks built the world's first communist state.
body:
The February revolution ended the monarchy; the [October revolution](event:october-revolution) put Lenin in power; a civil war of five years followed, and the [Soviet Union](event:ussr-founded) was formed in 1922.

It made [communism](event:communist-manifesto) a governing ideology and set up the [Cold War](event:cold-war) that dominated the century's second half.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Revolution).

name: October Revolution
summary: Bolshevik forces seized the Winter Palace and the organs of the Provisional Government in Petrograd.
body:
Part of [Russian Revolution](event:russian-revolution). Bolshevik forces seized the Winter Palace and the organs of the Provisional Government in Petrograd.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October_Revolution).

name: Soviet Union founded
summary: The union treaty created the USSR, which would last until [1991](event:soviet-collapse).
body:
Part of [Russian Revolution](event:russian-revolution). The union treaty created the USSR, which would last until [1991](event:soviet-collapse).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union).

name: Spanish flu pandemic
summary: An H1N1 influenza pandemic infected perhaps a third of humanity and killed 50 million or more.
body:
It spread along the troop movements of [the First World War](event:ww1), and unusually killed healthy young adults. Wartime censorship kept it out of the news everywhere except neutral Spain — hence the misleading name.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_flu).

name: Discovery of penicillin
summary: Alexander Fleming noticed that a stray mould killed bacteria on a forgotten culture plate.
body:
Mass production from 1943 gave medicine its first reliable cure for bacterial infection and saved uncounted millions of lives.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penicillin).

name: Great Depression
summary: The deepest economic collapse of the industrial age: a quarter of American workers unemployed, world trade down by two thirds.
body:
It began with the [Wall Street crash](event:wall-street-crash), spread through the gold standard and banking failures, and produced both the New Deal and the political conditions for [fascism in Europe](event:ww2).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression).

name: Wall Street crash
summary: The New York stock market lost a third of its value in weeks, wiping out fortunes and confidence alike.
body:
Part of [Great Depression](event:great-depression). The New York stock market lost a third of its value in weeks, wiping out fortunes and confidence alike.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wall_Street_Crash_of_1929).

name: The Dust Bowl
summary: Drought and ploughed-up prairie grass turned the southern Great Plains into moving dunes, displacing hundreds of thousands.
body:
Part of [Great Depression](event:great-depression). Drought and ploughed-up prairie grass turned the southern Great Plains into moving dunes, displacing hundreds of thousands.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dust_Bowl).

name: Gandhi's Salt March
summary: Gandhi walked 385 km to the sea to make salt in defiance of the British monopoly, launching mass civil disobedience.
body:
Part of [British Raj](event:british-raj). His method of non-violent resistance directly influenced the [American civil rights movement](event:civil-rights).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_March).

name: Spanish Civil War
summary: Franco's nationalists, backed by Germany and Italy, defeated the Republic; the war served as a rehearsal for [the world war](event:ww2).
body:
Franco's nationalists, backed by Germany and Italy, defeated the Republic; the war served as a rehearsal for [the world war](event:ww2).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Civil_War).

name: World War II
summary: The deadliest conflict in history: some 70–85 million dead, fought across every ocean and most continents.
body:
Germany's invasion of Poland began it in Europe; [Barbarossa](event:barbarossa) and [Pearl Harbor](event:pearl-harbor) in 1941 made it global. The tide turned at [Stalingrad](event:stalingrad) and [Midway](event:midway); [D-Day](event:d-day) opened the Western Front; the [Holocaust](event:holocaust) murdered six million Jews.

It ended with the [atomic bombing of Hiroshima](event:hiroshima) weeks after the [Trinity test](event:trinity), opening the nuclear age and the [Cold War](event:cold-war) that followed.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II).

image.caption: US troops landing at Omaha Beach, 1944

name: Battle of Britain
summary: The RAF held off the Luftwaffe in the first campaign fought entirely in the air, ending the threat of invasion.
body:
Part of [World War II](event:ww2). The RAF held off the Luftwaffe in the first campaign fought entirely in the air, ending the threat of invasion.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Britain).

name: Operation Barbarossa
summary: Germany invaded the Soviet Union along a 2,900 km front — the largest invasion in history.
body:
Part of [World War II](event:ww2). Germany invaded the Soviet Union along a 2,900 km front — the largest invasion in history.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Barbarossa).

name: Attack on Pearl Harbor
summary: A Japanese carrier strike on the US Pacific Fleet brought the United States into the war.
body:
Part of [World War II](event:ww2). A Japanese carrier strike on the US Pacific Fleet brought the United States into the war.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_on_Pearl_Harbor).

name: The Holocaust
summary: Nazi Germany murdered six million Jews, along with Roma, disabled people, Soviet prisoners and political opponents.
body:
Part of [World War II](event:ww2). Mass shootings by the Einsatzgruppen gave way to industrialised killing at extermination camps, of which Auschwitz-Birkenau was the largest. The word *genocide* was coined to describe it, and the Genocide Convention of 1948 followed.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Holocaust).

name: Battle of Stalingrad
summary: The turning point of the Eastern Front; the German Sixth Army was encircled and destroyed in the ruined city.
body:
Part of [World War II](event:ww2). Roughly **two million** casualties made it one of the bloodiest battles in history. The Soviet counter-offensive *Operation Uranus* closed the ring in November 1942; Paulus surrendered in February.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Stalingrad).

name: Battle of Midway
summary: American carriers sank four Japanese fleet carriers in a single day, reversing the balance in the Pacific.
body:
Part of [World War II](event:ww2). American carriers sank four Japanese fleet carriers in a single day, reversing the balance in the Pacific.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Midway).

name: D-Day landings
summary: The largest amphibious operation ever mounted put 156,000 Allied troops ashore in Normandy in one day.
body:
Part of [World War II](event:ww2). The largest amphibious operation ever mounted put 156,000 Allied troops ashore in Normandy in one day.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normandy_landings).

name: Trinity nuclear test
summary: The first detonation of a nuclear weapon, in the New Mexico desert before dawn on 16 July 1945.
body:
Part of [World War II](event:ww2). The product of the Manhattan Project, it made the [bombing of Hiroshima](event:hiroshima) possible three weeks later.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinity_(nuclear_test)).

name: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
summary: Two atomic bombs killed well over 100,000 people; Japan surrendered within days.
body:
Part of [World War II](event:ww2). They remain the only use of nuclear weapons in war. The threat of their use structured the entire [Cold War](event:cold-war).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_bombings_of_Hiroshima_and_Nagasaki).

name: United Nations founded
summary: Fifty states signed the UN Charter in San Francisco, creating a permanent forum and a Security Council with teeth on paper.
body:
The Universal Declaration of Human Rights followed in 1948.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations).

name: Decolonisation
summary: Within thirty years of the Second World War, the European overseas empires dissolved into some seventy new states.
body:
It began with [India](event:indian-independence) in 1947 and accelerated through Africa after 1957; some transitions were negotiated, others — Algeria, Vietnam, Angola — were long wars.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decolonization).

name: Independence of India and Pakistan
summary: Britain withdrew from South Asia, and the subcontinent was divided into two states.
body:
Part of [Decolonisation](event:decolonisation). Independence was the culmination of decades of mass campaigning, including [Gandhi's Salt March](event:salt-march). [Partition](event:partition) accompanied it: 10–20 million displaced and perhaps a million killed.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_independence_movement).

name: Partition of India
summary: Hastily drawn borders through Punjab and Bengal triggered the largest mass migration in history and appalling communal violence.
body:
Part of [Independence of India and Pakistan](event:indian-independence). Hastily drawn borders through Punjab and Bengal triggered the largest mass migration in history and appalling communal violence.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partition_of_India).

name: Founding of the State of Israel
summary: Israel declared independence as the British mandate ended; war with its Arab neighbours followed immediately, displacing some 700,000 Palestinians.
body:
Israel declared independence as the British mandate ended; war with its Arab neighbours followed immediately, displacing some 700,000 Palestinians.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Declaration_of_Independence).

name: People's Republic of China proclaimed
summary: Mao Zedong declared the PRC from Tiananmen after the Communist victory in the civil war.
body:
The following decades brought land reform, the famine of the Great Leap Forward, the [Cultural Revolution](event:cultural-revolution) and, after 1978, the reforms that made China the world's second-largest economy.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proclamation_of_the_People%27s_Republic_of_China).

name: The Cold War
summary: For forty-four years the United States and the Soviet Union confronted each other everywhere except in direct battle.
body:
It ran through the [Berlin blockade](event:berlin-blockade), [Korea](event:korean-war), the [Cuban Missile Crisis](event:cuban-missile-crisis) — the closest the world has come to nuclear war — [Vietnam](event:vietnam-war), and the [Berlin Wall](event:berlin-wall).

It also drove the [Space Race](event:space-race). It ended with the [fall of the Wall](event:berlin-wall-fall) and the [collapse of the Soviet Union](event:soviet-collapse).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War).

name: Berlin Blockade and Airlift
summary: The Soviets cut off West Berlin; Allied aircraft supplied the city for eleven months.
body:
Part of [The Cold War](event:cold-war). The Soviets cut off West Berlin; Allied aircraft supplied the city for eleven months.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Blockade).

name: Korean War
summary: North Korean, Chinese, American and UN forces fought to a stalemate close to the original border; no peace treaty was ever signed.
body:
Part of [The Cold War](event:cold-war). North Korean, Chinese, American and UN forces fought to a stalemate close to the original border; no peace treaty was ever signed.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_War).

name: Berlin Wall built
summary: East Germany walled off West Berlin overnight to stop the flight of its population.
body:
Part of [The Cold War](event:cold-war). East Germany walled off West Berlin overnight to stop the flight of its population.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Wall).

name: Cuban Missile Crisis
summary: Thirteen days in October 1962 brought the superpowers closer to nuclear war than at any other moment.
body:
Part of [The Cold War](event:cold-war). Soviet missiles in Cuba were withdrawn in exchange for a US pledge not to invade and the quiet removal of American missiles from Turkey. A direct Moscow–Washington hotline followed.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_Missile_Crisis).

name: Vietnam War
summary: Two decades of war ended with American withdrawal and the unification of Vietnam under the north.
body:
Part of [The Cold War](event:cold-war). Perhaps three million Vietnamese died. Televised coverage and mass protest changed how Western democracies relate to their own wars.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War).

name: Fall of the Berlin Wall
summary: A confused press conference on 9 November sent crowds to the checkpoints, and the guards let them through.
body:
Part of [The Cold War](event:cold-war). Within a year Germany was reunified; within two the [Soviet Union](event:soviet-collapse) had dissolved. Communist governments across Eastern Europe fell in the same few months.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fall_of_the_Berlin_Wall).

name: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
summary: The USSR broke into fifteen independent states and the Cold War ended without a shot fired between the superpowers.
body:
Part of [The Cold War](event:cold-war). Gorbachev's reforms, nationalist movements in the republics and a failed hard-line coup in August 1991 brought down the state founded by the [October Revolution](event:october-revolution).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dissolution_of_the_Soviet_Union).

name: Invention of the transistor
summary: Bell Labs built a solid-state amplifier and switch, the component from which all modern electronics is made.
body:
Shrinking transistors — from one per device to tens of billions on a [chip](event:microprocessor) — is the single trend behind computing, communications and the [internet](event:internet).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transistor).

name: Structure of DNA
summary: Watson and Crick, using Rosalind Franklin's X-ray data, described the double helix — and with it, how genes copy themselves.
body:
Molecular biology, genetic engineering, [the Human Genome Project](event:human-genome) and [CRISPR](event:crispr) all follow from this two-page paper.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid_double_helix).

name: The Space Race
summary: The superpowers competed to reach orbit, then the Moon, in a contest of prestige with military roots.
body:
Part of [The Cold War](event:cold-war). It ran from [Sputnik](event:sputnik) through [Gagarin](event:gagarin) to the [Apollo programme](event:apollo-program), and ended symbolically with a US–Soviet docking in orbit in 1975.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Race).

name: Sputnik 1
summary: The first artificial satellite beeped overhead every 96 minutes and stunned the United States into action.
body:
Part of [The Space Race](event:space-race). The first artificial satellite beeped overhead every 96 minutes and stunned the United States into action.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sputnik_1).

name: Yuri Gagarin orbits the Earth
summary: The first human in space completed a single orbit aboard Vostok 1 and landed by parachute.
body:
Part of [The Space Race](event:space-race). The first human in space completed a single orbit aboard Vostok 1 and landed by parachute.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuri_Gagarin).

name: Apollo programme
summary: Kennedy's commitment to land a man on the Moon before the decade was out mobilised 400,000 people and 4% of the federal budget.
body:
Part of [The Space Race](event:space-race). Kennedy's commitment to land a man on the Moon before the decade was out mobilised 400,000 people and 4% of the federal budget.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_program).

name: Apollo 11 Moon landing
summary: Humans walked on another world for the first time; some 600 million people watched.
body:
Part of [Apollo programme](event:apollo-program). *That's one small step for a man, one giant leap for mankind.* Armstrong and Aldrin spent 21 hours on the Sea of Tranquillity while Collins orbited above.

It was the culmination of the [Space Race](event:space-race), and the furthest humans have yet travelled.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11).

image.caption: Buzz Aldrin on the lunar surface

name: Apollo 13
summary: An oxygen tank exploded on the way to the Moon; the crew improvised their way home in the lunar module.
body:
Part of [Apollo programme](event:apollo-program). An oxygen tank exploded on the way to the Moon; the crew improvised their way home in the lunar module.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_13).

name: Voyager probes launched
summary: Two spacecraft toured the outer planets and are now the most distant human-made objects, in interstellar space.
body:
Two spacecraft toured the outer planets and are now the most distant human-made objects, in interstellar space.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voyager_program).

name: Green Revolution
summary: High-yield dwarf wheat and rice, fertiliser and irrigation roughly tripled cereal yields in the developing world.
body:
Norman Borlaug's varieties are credited with averting famine for a billion people, at the cost of heavy fertiliser and water use.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Revolution).

name: American civil rights movement
summary: A mass campaign of boycotts, marches and litigation dismantled legal segregation in the United States.
body:
From *Brown v. Board* and the Montgomery bus boycott through the [March on Washington](event:march-washington) to the [Civil Rights Act](event:civil-rights-act) and the Voting Rights Act, and the [assassination of Martin Luther King](event:mlk-assassination).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_rights_movement).

name: March on Washington
summary: A quarter of a million people gathered at the Lincoln Memorial to hear King's "I Have a Dream" speech.
body:
Part of [American civil rights movement](event:civil-rights). A quarter of a million people gathered at the Lincoln Memorial to hear King's "I Have a Dream" speech.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_on_Washington_for_Jobs_and_Freedom).

name: Civil Rights Act of 1964
summary: Federal law outlawed discrimination by race, colour, religion, sex or national origin in employment and public accommodation.
body:
Part of [American civil rights movement](event:civil-rights). Federal law outlawed discrimination by race, colour, religion, sex or national origin in employment and public accommodation.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_Rights_Act_of_1964).

name: Assassination of Martin Luther King Jr.
summary: King was shot in Memphis while supporting a strike by sanitation workers; riots followed in over a hundred cities.
body:
Part of [American civil rights movement](event:civil-rights). King was shot in Memphis while supporting a strike by sanitation workers; riots followed in over a hundred cities.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Martin_Luther_King_Jr.).

name: Cultural Revolution
summary: Mao mobilised students against the party and the "four olds"; universities closed, millions were persecuted and much cultural heritage was destroyed.
body:
Part of [People's Republic of China proclaimed](event:prc-founded). Mao mobilised students against the party and the "four olds"; universities closed, millions were persecuted and much cultural heritage was destroyed.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_Revolution).

name: ARPANET and the Internet
summary: The first packet-switched network linked four American universities; TCP/IP made networks of networks possible.
body:
It carried email, then the [World Wide Web](event:www), and now most of human communication and commerce.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARPANET).

name: The microprocessor
summary: Intel put a whole central processing unit on one chip, making computers cheap enough to be everywhere.
body:
Part of [Invention of the transistor](event:transistor). Intel put a whole central processing unit on one chip, making computers cheap enough to be everywhere.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microprocessor).

name: Eradication of smallpox
summary: The WHO declared smallpox eradicated — the only human disease ever deliberately eliminated.
body:
A worldwide campaign of surveillance and ring [vaccination](event:smallpox-vaccine) ended a disease that had killed an estimated 300 million people in the twentieth century alone.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smallpox).

name: Chernobyl disaster
summary: A reactor test went catastrophically wrong, spreading radioactive fallout across Europe and forcing permanent evacuation.
body:
The accident damaged Soviet credibility at home and abroad and reshaped nuclear policy worldwide.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chernobyl_disaster).

name: Montreal Protocol
summary: Every country agreed to phase out CFCs to protect the ozone layer — the most successful environmental treaty yet made.
body:
The ozone hole is now measurably healing, and the treaty avoided a great deal of additional [warming](event:global-warming) as well.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montreal_Protocol).

name: World Wide Web
summary: Tim Berners-Lee proposed a hypertext system at CERN; it became the way most of humanity gets information.
body:
URLs, HTTP and HTML were released royalty-free in 1993, a decision that let the Web grow without a gatekeeper. Built on the [Internet](event:internet), it took the number of connected users from thousands to billions in two decades.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Wide_Web).

name: Maastricht Treaty and the European Union
summary: The European Communities became the European Union, with a common currency to follow in 1999.
body:
The European Communities became the European Union, with a common currency to follow in 1999.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maastricht_Treaty).

name: Rwandan genocide
summary: Some 800,000 Tutsi and moderate Hutu were murdered in a hundred days while the world looked away.
body:
Some 800,000 Tutsi and moderate Hutu were murdered in a hundred days while the world looked away.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rwandan_genocide).

name: End of apartheid in South Africa
summary: Nelson Mandela, imprisoned for 27 years, was elected president in the country's first universal-suffrage election.
body:
The negotiated transition and the Truth and Reconciliation Commission avoided the civil war many had predicted.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apartheid).

name: September 11 attacks
summary: Hijacked airliners destroyed the World Trade Center and struck the Pentagon, killing nearly 3,000 people.
body:
The attacks triggered the wars in Afghanistan and Iraq, a global expansion of surveillance, and two decades of security policy still in force.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks).

name: Human Genome Project completed
summary: Thirteen years and three billion base pairs later, the human genetic sequence was published and placed in the public domain.
body:
Sequencing a genome cost about a billion dollars in 2003 and a few hundred today — one of the fastest cost collapses in the history of technology. See also [CRISPR](event:crispr).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_Genome_Project).

name: The smartphone era
summary: The iPhone put a networked computer with a camera in a pocket, and within a decade most of humanity carried one.
body:
The iPhone put a networked computer with a camera in a pocket, and within a decade most of humanity carried one.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPhone_(1st_generation)).

name: Global financial crisis
summary: The collapse of the American mortgage market brought down banks worldwide and caused the deepest recession since the 1930s.
body:
The collapse of the American mortgage market brought down banks worldwide and caused the deepest recession since the 1930s.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007–2008_financial_crisis).

name: Arab Spring
summary: Protests spread from Tunisia across the Arab world, toppling four governments and setting off civil wars in Syria, Libya and Yemen.
body:
Protests spread from Tunisia across the Arab world, toppling four governments and setting off civil wars in Syria, Libya and Yemen.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_Spring).

name: Discovery of the Higgs boson
summary: The LHC at CERN found the particle that completes the Standard Model and explains how other particles acquire mass.
body:
The LHC at CERN found the particle that completes the Standard Model and explains how other particles acquire mass.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higgs_boson).

name: CRISPR gene editing
summary: A bacterial immune system was turned into a cheap, precise tool for editing the DNA of any organism.
body:
Doudna and Charpentier shared the 2020 Nobel Prize; the first approved CRISPR therapy, for sickle-cell disease, arrived in 2023. See [DNA](event:dna-structure).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CRISPR_gene_editing).

name: First detection of gravitational waves
summary: LIGO recorded spacetime ripples from two merging black holes, a century after [Einstein](event:relativity) predicted them.
body:
LIGO recorded spacetime ripples from two merging black holes, a century after [Einstein](event:relativity) predicted them.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_observation_of_gravitational_waves).

name: Paris Agreement on climate change
summary: Nearly every country agreed to limit warming to well below 2 °C, with national pledges rather than binding quotas.
body:
It is the main international response to [modern global warming](event:global-warming).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Agreement).

name: Modern global warming
summary: Greenhouse gases released since the Industrial Revolution have warmed the planet by about 1.3 °C, and the rate is increasing.
body:
Atmospheric CO2 has risen from about 280 ppm before the [Industrial Revolution](event:industrial-revolution) to over 420 ppm. Ice sheets and glaciers are losing mass, sea level is rising, and extreme heat has become measurably more frequent.

The [Montreal Protocol](event:montreal-protocol) and the [Paris Agreement](event:paris-agreement) are the main treaty responses; the geological analogue is the [PETM](event:petm), 56 million years ago.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_warming).

name: Deep learning and modern AI
summary: Neural networks trained on large datasets went from academic curiosity to general-purpose technology in about a decade.
body:
AlexNet's 2012 win in an image-recognition contest started the boom; transformer models from 2017 led to systems that write, translate, code and reason across domains.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_learning).

name: COVID-19 pandemic
summary: A novel coronavirus spread worldwide within months, killing an estimated 7–27 million people and shutting down much of the global economy.
body:
It produced the fastest vaccine development in history: mRNA vaccines were in arms within a year of the virus being sequenced. Comparisons were drawn throughout to the [1918 influenza pandemic](event:spanish-flu).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic).

name: James Webb Space Telescope
summary: A 6.5-metre infrared telescope launched to a point 1.5 million km from Earth to observe the first galaxies.
body:
A 6.5-metre infrared telescope launched to a point 1.5 million km from Earth to observe the first galaxies.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope).

name: Russian invasion of Ukraine
summary: Russia launched the largest land war in Europe since 1945, driving millions from their homes and reshaping European security.
body:
Russia launched the largest land war in Europe since 1945, driving millions from their homes and reshaping European security.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine).

name: World population reaches 8 billion
summary: The UN marked an eightfold increase in human numbers since 1800, with growth now slowing worldwide.
body:
The UN marked an eightfold increase in human numbers since 1800, with growth now slowing worldwide.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_population).
